newsitem.title: USA: U.S Justice official defends withholding drug memo.
newsitem.headline: U.S Justice official defends withholding drug memo.

text.p: A Justice Department official Thursday rejected Republican political criticism over the White House's decision to withhold from Congress a confidential 1995 memo on the Clinton administration's drug policy.

Deputy Attorney General Jamie Gorelick also denied that the memo -- written by FBI Director Louis Freeh and Drug Enforcement Administration chief Thomas Constantine -- attacked President Clinton's leadership in fighting illegal drugs.

Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, at a campaign appearance Wednesday in Pennsylvania, demanded that Clinton release the memo. "Mr. President, it is time to release this memo so that the American people can see how bad your drug policy has been over the past 44 months."
The White House invoked executive privilege in refusing to turn over the memo to a Republican-controlled House panel.
Gorelick cited opinions by a Reagan Justice Department official and former Republican Attorney General Dick Thornburgh that executive privilege can be asserted for such internal government memos.
Thornburgh was scheduled to join Republican National Committee Chairman Haley Barbour at a news conference later Thursday concerning the memo.
Gorelick told the weekly Justice Department news conference that the White House did not need a "dramatic national security issue" to invoke executive privilege.
"I think that what the privilege does is try to protect the fundamental ability of the president to function," she said.

"If a president cannot ... have a confidential communication or cannot receive such a communication in writing, if such communications are open to review by Congress or the public, I think it undermines the ability of the executive branch to function," Gorelick said.
Asked if the memo involved concerns over coordination among various government agencies in fighting drugs, Gorelick replied that Clinton has taken a number of steps.
She said Clinton restructured the White House drug czar's office to improve coordination and that Attorney General Janet Reno has taken a "stronger leadership role" among law enforcement agencies.
She said the memo was sent to Clinton by Reno and that the Justice Department had been consulted about the executive privilege claim.
